audit_notes: AUDIT FAILED - REQUEST PHYSICALLY IMPOSSIBLE. The original user requirement (a surface in a fully closed, adiabatic system with no energy input that permanently delivers more heat than it receives, efficiency > 300 %, heating a house) violates the first law of thermodynamics: with no heat or work crossing the boundary, the internal energy is constant and no sustained net heat output to a house is possible (perpetuum mobile of the first kind). A house outside an adiabatic boundary by definition cannot receive heat from it. No parameter adjustment can resolve this, so the design cannot be accepted as a solution of the stated request. Technical check of the proposed SUBSTITUTE model (open-system heat-pump evaporator fin, 1D fin equation with insulated tip): all parameters are positive and within realistic bounds (Al fin t=0.2 mm, L=20 mm, pitch 2 mm > t, k=205 W/mK, h=50 W/m2K, dT=8 K). m^2 L^2 = 2 h L^2/(k t) = 0.976, mL = 0.988, fin efficiency tanh(mL)/mL = 0.766, Biot (half thickness) = 2.4e-5 so the 1D assumption holds. Heat per unit fin width q = k t (m/L) theta0 tanh(mL) ~ 12.3 W/m. No structural or thermal limits are exceeded (evaporator temperatures far below Al limits). This substitute model conserves energy; the heat comes from ambient air plus compressor work, so it is NOT a closed adiabatic system and a COP > 3 from it must not be reported as fulfilling the user's request. Recommendation: reject the request as stated and tell the user it is impossible; if they accept an open system, reformulate as a heat-pump COP optimization.
